macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Oil and geopolitics dominate markets as fresh U.S. strikes on Iran rattle investors
items.summary: Reuters reports that U.S. stock futures edged higher after global markets and oil prices steadied, following renewed U.S. strikes on Iran that revived geopolitical anxiety and threatened to prolong the conflict. Reuters also said Asian shares rose but were capped by an oil-price surge that reignited inflation fears, while European stocks gained in choppy trade as investors watched the Middle East situation.

items.title: Fed caution and inflation concerns temper risk appetite in global equities
items.summary: MarketScreener highlighted that Australian shares wobbled as caution from the Federal Reserve offset some of the optimism from lower oil prices. Reuters also noted a broader inflation-sensitive backdrop, including China's producer prices rising to a near four-year high and India’s inflation likely moving above the RBI’s 4% target.

items.title: IMF warns the Iran shock is worsening the global inflation outlook
items.summary: The Financial Times reported that the IMF sees inflation risk looming large over the global economy and has raised its projections for price growth. Al Jazeera separately reported that the IMF cut its 2026 world growth forecast, citing fallout from the Iran war and the energy shock.

items.title: Reuters says some Fed officials still saw the need for future rate rises
items.summary: The Financial Times reported that minutes from the Federal Reserve's last meeting showed some officials believed further rate increases may be needed to contain inflation. That reinforces a hawkish policy backdrop even as markets continue to price changing odds for the next Fed move.

items.title: Japan bond yields hit 30-year high as oil and inflation fears rise
items.summary: Reuters said the benchmark 10-year Japanese government bond yield reached a 30-year high as higher oil prices renewed inflation concerns and investors remained wary of Japan's fiscal outlook. Bloomberg also reported that Japanese bank lending is rising fast enough to support the Bank of Japan's path toward further rate hikes.

items.title: China inflation data shows persistent cost pressure
items.summary: Reuters reported that China's producer price inflation rose to its highest level since July 2022, while consumer prices also continued to rise. That points to persistent cost pressures for manufacturers even as broader growth concerns remain.

items.title: Indian inflation and growth concerns remain in focus
items.summary: Reuters said India's consumer inflation likely breached the RBI's 4% target in June for the first time in 16 months, driven by food, fuel, the Iran war, and weak monsoon conditions. Business Standard and Moneycontrol also pointed to softer activity data, lower reserves, and pressure on the rupee.

items.title: OPEC+ agrees modest August output increase as crude remains a central market driver
items.summary: Yahoo Finance reported that seven OPEC+ countries agreed to lift combined oil output by 188,000 barrels per day in August. The move adds supply, but oil remains a key market driver after the Iran-related spike in prices.

items.title: Ford's Q2 earnings beat lifts outlook
items.summary: Yahoo Finance reported that Ford's Q2 automotive revenue came in at $44.9 billion, slightly above expectations, and that the company lifted its outlook after the earnings beat. This makes Ford one of the notable company-specific earnings stories in the latest coverage.

items.title: Global equity tone mixed, with tech and semiconductors driving volatility
items.summary: Reuters and Bloomberg said technology and semiconductor shares were central to the latest swings in Asian and European markets, with gains in some areas offset by weakness in others. Bloomberg described Asian stocks as poised to drop for a second day amid a chipmaker selloff tied to the oil and Iran shock.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Work for workplace automation
items.summary: OpenAI unveiled ChatGPT Work, an agent designed to execute tasks across apps and files, intensifying competition in professional AI tools. The move is part of a broader push toward workplace automation and enterprise adoption.

items.title: OpenAI releases GPT-Live, a real-time voice model family
items.summary: OpenAI launched GPT-Live, a new family of voice models that can listen and speak simultaneously in real time. The release expands the company’s multimodal and conversational AI lineup.

items.title: Meta opens developer access to Muse Spark 1.1
items.summary: Meta released developer access to its Muse Spark AI model and an upgraded version, positioning it against paid AI offerings from rivals such as Anthropic and OpenAI. The release signals a stronger push into model access for developers.

items.title: OpenAI faces renewed copyright pressure in New York case
items.summary: Several newspapers, including The New York Times and New York Daily News, asked a federal court to sanction OpenAI over alleged misstatements about searching its systems for evidence of training misuse. The dispute adds to the legal risk around AI training data.

items.title: Anthropic adds Ben Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust
items.summary: Anthropic appointed former U.S. Federal Reserve chair Ben Bernanke to its oversight trust, which is meant to help ensure the company stays aligned with its public mission. The appointment underscores continued governance and safety positioning in frontier AI.

items.title: Character.AI fined by Italy’s data protection authority
items.summary: Italy fined Character Technologies €158,000 for breaches of data protection rules involving Character.AI. The penalty highlights ongoing regulatory scrutiny of consumer AI platforms and data handling practices.

items.title: Grok 4.5 launched for coding and agentic tasks
items.summary: SpaceXAI launched Grok 4.5, describing it as its most intelligent model yet and aiming it at coding and agentic workflows. The release adds to the rapid pace of model launches in the frontier AI market.

items.title: Micron announces more than $250 billion U.S. investment tied to AI demand
items.summary: Micron said it plans to invest more than $250 billion in the U.S. through 2035, citing surging memory-chip demand in the AI era. The announcement reflects how AI infrastructure spending is reshaping the semiconductor industry.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Xbox Game Pass growth reportedly fell far short of Microsoft’s targets
items.summary: Reports say Microsoft expected Game Pass to reach 77 million subscribers by now, but it is reportedly around 30 million, with Xbox leadership admitting the strategy has not grown as planned.

items.title: Sony says new PlayStation games will go digital-only starting in 2028
items.summary: Sony has reportedly confirmed it will end physical disc production for new PlayStation titles in January 2028, signaling a major shift toward digital distribution on PS5 and beyond.

items.title: Nintendo confirms Mario Kart Tour shutdown after 7 years
items.summary: Nintendo will discontinue Mario Kart Tour in September and will not offer an offline version, ending the mobile racer’s run after seven years.

items.title: Fortnite returns to the US Apple App Store
items.summary: BBC News reports that Fortnite is back on the US Apple App Store after the ban was lifted, restoring access for iPhone users in the U.S.

items.title: Call of Duty: Black Ops 1 and 2 ports now available on PS5
items.summary: Call of Duty: Black Ops and Black Ops 2 are now available on PS4 and PS5, though reports note the ports come at a high price.

items.title: Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced hits a major Steam player peak
items.summary: The newly released Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced reportedly reached around 100,000 concurrent players on Steam, marking the biggest player peak in the franchise to date.

items.title: Pokémon Go marks its 10th anniversary with a livestream
items.summary: Pokémon Go is celebrating its 10th anniversary today with a special livestream focused on announcements and surprises for players.

items.title: Epic Games settles lawsuit with former Fortnite leaker
items.summary: Epic Games has reportedly settled its lawsuit against former contractor Hayden Cohen over alleged leaks of confidential Fortnite collaboration details, dropping its monetary claims.

items.title: Nintendo’s Splatoon Raiders Direct reveals new game details
items.summary: Nintendo shared fresh news in a Splatoon Raiders Direct presentation, confirming the game will launch exclusively on Nintendo Switch 2 on July 23.

items.title: Sony outlines end of physical discs for PlayStation
items.summary: Sony has clarified that production of physical game discs for new PlayStation titles will end in January 2028, with future releases sold digitally.
